Projects and Workspaces

This page introduces how SLA / SA projects are organized: the two forms of the sa.mod manifest (single package and multi-member workspace), the managed cache directory .sla-cache/, and how the demos/ example directory is organized. After reading it you will be able to understand and set up a multi-package project.

sa.mod: The Package Manifest

The minimal manifest generated by sla init (equivalent to sa sla init) is a single declaration line:

# generated by sla init
package "sla_app"

sa.mod is also the vehicle for workspaces on the SA side. sci's workspace demo (demos/workspace/sa.mod) shows the complete form:

workspace {
  members ["members/app", "members/tool"]
  default_member "app"
}
FieldDescription
workspace { … }Declares the root sa.mod as a multi-member workspace
members […]The list of member directories; each member has its own sa.mod (containing its own package "…") and src/
default_member "…"The member built/checked by default when -p is not specified; can be matched by path or package name

The SLA plugin parses the workspace members of the current sa.mod: sla sab workspace (equivalent to sa sla sab workspace) goes through the managed SAB compilation and then delegates to sa build-exe; use -p <package> to select a member, and --sab-out <file.sab> to additionally write out an artifact for inspection. When no member is specified and there is only one member, that member is selected automatically.

NoteWorkspace source resolution on the SLA side is built on sa.mod; for a reference example see sa_plugin_sla's demos/workspace/ (with the two members members/app and members/tool).

.sla-cache: The Managed Cache Directory

  • Managed SAB artifacts live under .sla-cache/sab/…; unchanged SAB bytes are not rewritten, so that SA's incremental cache can reuse stable inputs.
  • Filtered test builds use filter-scoped paths and do not overwrite the SAB artifacts of ordinary build/workspace runs.
  • User-visible SAB files are written only when --out / --sab-out / --emit-sab is passed explicitly.
  • The directory is automatically written into the project's .gitignore by sa sla init; do not commit it to version control.

How the demos Directory Is Organized

sci/demos/ is the end-to-end example tree:

SubdirectoryContents
rosetta/A numbered sample set (01_hello_world, 05_struct, 117_inline_assembly, etc.) mirroring the Rust reference implementations with comparison notes; the SLA counterparts are in sa_plugin_sla's demos/rosetta/
workspace/A demonstration of native sa.mod workspace support
cli_workflows/Documentation demonstrating CLI usage such as explain, fix --plan, layout, and skills
compare/, support/, bc2sa_cmakeComparison benchmarks, trap/support fixtures, and a bc2sa build example
WarningReference artifacts such as main.sa in the demo directories are git-tracked files. When batch compiling, do not use --out to write output next to the source directory, lest you overwrite the reference artifacts; if you overwrite one by mistake, restore it with git checkout -- demos.

A Typical Layout

my_app/
├── sa.mod              # package "my_app"（或 workspace 声明）
├── .gitignore          # 忽略 .sla-cache/ 等
└── src/
    └── main.sla        # 入口：fn main() -> i32

For more CLI details, see the sa sla sab workspace entry in the Command-Line Reference chapter.
